extracted.intended_audience: Title IX coordinators, school and college administrators, legal counsel, and other officials at educational institutions receiving Federal financial assistance
extracted.subtask_short: Title IX grievance procedures for recipients
extracted.subtask_description: Clarifications and requirements for how recipients (elementary, secondary, and postsecondary educational institutions) must conduct grievance procedures under Title IX, including notice, remedies, appeals, and limits on discipline. Focuses on procedural safeguards and responsibilities of the Title IX Coordinator and the institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written notification of determination whether sex discrimination occurred (§106.45(h)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must provide parties (complainant and respondent) written notification of the determination whether sex discrimination occurred under Title IX or this part and must include the rationale for that determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department revised §106.45(h)(2) to require written notification to ensure transparency and consistency and to provide parties the information necessary to utilize their right to appeal. Written notification requirement applies to elementary and secondary recipients as well as postsecondary institutions (although elementary/secondary recipients need not provide the same level of detail as postsecondary §106.46(h)). Recipients must ensure such notice complies with IDEA and/or Section 504 when applicable. The notice must also include procedures and permissible bases for appeal, if applicable, consistent with §106.45(i). The Department relied on existing recordkeeping obligations (§106.8(f)(1)) in concluding this imposes limited additional burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal process equivalence (§106.45(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must offer an appeal process from a determination arising out of a sex discrimination complaint that is the same as the appeal process the recipient offers in other comparable proceedings, if any.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department modified §106.45(i) to require recipients to offer appeals at least equal to those in comparable proceedings. Recipients have discretion to define the bases for appeal, and parties may only appeal on the bases the recipient provides. The appeals process should be carefully delineated to limit abuse; appeals do not permit reasons beyond those set by the recipient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title IX Coordinator must coordinate provision and implementation of remedies (§106.45(h)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Title IX Coordinator's role is to coordinate the provision and implementation of remedies (rather than to personally provide and implement them). The recipient remains ultimately responsible for compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipient may delegate duties (§106.8(a)(2)) to personnel best positioned to perform tasks and avoid conflicts of interest. Remedies can only be provided after a recipient determines sex discrimination occurred, and must be designed to restore or preserve access to the recipient's education program or activity (see §106.2 definition of 'remedies'). Examples: transcript changes must be coordinated through the registrar; counseling remedies must be coordinated through counseling resources. The Coordinator is also responsible for coordinating implementation of disciplinary sanctions and notifying the complainant of such sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedies may extend to complainant and other persons (§106.45(h)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: When sex discrimination is determined, a recipient may need to provide remedies to the complainant and other persons identified by the recipient as having had equal access limited or denied by sex discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Language changed from 'or other person' to 'and other persons' to recognize that multiple individuals may require remedies (example: other students in a club who experienced the same hostile environment). Recipients are not required to notify respondents of remedies that impose no action on the respondent. Remedies may be limited by practical constraints (e.g., graduation) though some remedies may still be appropriate after graduation. The final regulations do not require identifying a list of particular remedies and permit recipients discretion in selecting remedies that restore or preserve access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supportive measures available regardless of determination (§106.44(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must offer and coordinate supportive measures to protect safety or provide support during grievance procedures; supportive measures may be offered even if the recipient does not determine that sex discrimination occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supportive measures must not unreasonably burden either party, may not be punitive or disciplinary, and are designed to protect safety or the educational environment or to provide support during grievance procedures (or informal resolution). Examples include no-contact orders, schedule adjustments, counseling referrals. Supportive measures cannot be provided for punitive reasons because a determination has not yet been made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency removal criteria (§106.44(h))
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient may remove a respondent from the recipient's education program or activity on an emergency basis if an individualized safety and risk analysis determines that there is an imminent and serious threat to the health or safety of the complainant, students, employees, or other persons arising from the allegations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If removal occurs, recipient must provide the respondent with notice and an opportunity to challenge the decision immediately following the removal. Emergency removal is a non-disciplinary protective measure and can be used before a determination is reached, subject to the individualized safety/risk analysis requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative leave for employees during proceedings (§106.44(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient may place an employee respondent on administrative leave from employment responsibilities during the pendency of the recipient's grievance procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative leave is distinguished from disciplinary sanctions and is permissible while grievance procedures are pending. The recipient must manage such leaves consistent with the requirement to provide equitable treatment and to follow grievance procedures before imposing disciplinary sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comply with grievance procedures before imposing disciplinary sanctions (§106.45(h)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must follow the grievance procedures in §106.45 before imposing any disciplinary sanctions or other actions that are not supportive measures against a respondent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement applies to all complaints of sex discrimination (not just sexual harassment) and is intended to ensure neutral, bias-free procedures. It balances expediency and fairness: recipients retain discretion regarding what disciplinary sanctions to impose but may not impose sanctions until procedures (including appeals, if applicable) are concluded. Recipients may use supportive measures, emergency removal, or administrative leave where appropriate before a final determination. State laws requiring action within a certain time may apply unless they conflict with these regulations (see §106.6(b)). The Department declines to require specific sanctions or to mandate reporting to State certification authorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on discipline based solely on determination whether discrimination occurred (§106.45(h)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may not discipline a party, witness, or other participant 'based solely' on the recipient's determination whether sex discrimination occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provision is intended to protect participation in grievance procedures by ensuring that the outcome alone cannot be the sole basis for disciplining someone for false statements. Recipients retain discretion to discipline those who make materially false statements made in bad faith, provided the discipline is based on evidence other than, or in addition to, the outcome of the grievance process. Evidence developed during the Title IX grievance may be used in a separate disciplinary process so long as the disciplinary action is not based solely on the outcome. Threatening or initiating disciplinary proceedings under certain circumstances could constitute retaliation under §106.71.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification to complainant of disciplinary sanctions imposed on respondent
rubrics_metrics.description: When disciplinary sanctions are imposed on a respondent following a determination that sex discrimination occurred, the Title IX Coordinator must notify the complainant of those disciplinary sanctions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department added language to §106.45(h)(3) to clarify this continuing requirement, reasoning that complainants should know what sanctions the respondent receives because knowledge of sanctions may impact the complainant's equal access to the education program or activity and may help prevent recurrence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of consensual sexual activity in relation to discipline (discussion under §106.45(h)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: Commenters raised concerns about disciplining individuals for consensual sexual conduct in the context of Title IX grievance procedures; some supported §106.45(h)(5) as protecting survivors from punishment related to consensual sexual activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department acknowledged commenters' concerns and noted awareness that some recipients have codes of conduct prohibiting consensual sexual conduct. Commenters suggested separating 'consensual sexual conduct' from 'false statements' for clarity; the Department did not adopt changes specifically mandating disciplinary rules for consensual sexual activity in this rulemaking, leaving recipients' codes of conduct and disciplinary processes in place subject to the limits of §106.45(h)(5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping/documentation supports written notice (§106.8(f)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients are already required to maintain documentation of the grievance procedures undertaken in response to a complaint of sex discrimination under §106.8(f)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department cited existing recordkeeping obligations to justify that requiring written notification of determinations and rationale will not impose significant additional burden, and to support the transparency rationale for written notice requirements.
